samples.text:
In many countries, the number of people who live alone is growing quickly. This essay will explain the reasons for this trend and discuss its effects on society.

There are several reasons why more people live alone. Firstly, people today get married later than in the past, and some decide not to marry at all. Young adults want to focus on their career and enjoy their freedom, so they rent a small flat by themselves. Secondly, many people move to big cities for work, far away from their parents, so they have no choice except living alone. Also, there are more elderly people now because people live longer, and when their husband or wife die, they often continue to live alone in their house. Finally, some people simply prefer privacy and independence.

This trend has both positive and negative effects on society. On the positive side, people who live alone often spend more money on restaurants, entertainment and travel, which is good for the economy. However, there are more negative effects. First, it increase the demand for housing, because one person needs a whole apartment, so house prices become higher. Second, many people who live alone feel lonely, especially old people, and this can cause health problems. For example, an elderly woman who lives by herself may not talk with anyone for several days. As a result, government have to spend more money on social services.

In conclusion, more people live alone because they marry later, move to cities for work and live longer. I believe this trend has more negative effects than positive, because it makes housing more expensive and causes loneliness in the society.
samples.why: Both questions answered with relevant reasons and effects · ideas stated simply with limited development · mechanical linking (Firstly, Also, First) · adequate vocabulary · errors in agreement and articles that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
Single-person households have become increasingly common in many parts of the world. This essay will examine the main reasons for this trend and consider its impact on society, which I believe is mixed but raises some serious concerns.

One of the most significant reasons is a change in social attitudes. In the past, young people usually stayed with their parents until they married, but today marriage often happens later or not at all, and living independently is seen as a normal stage of adult life. Economic growth has also made this possible, since many young professionals earn enough to rent their own apartment. Another factor is the ageing population. As life expectancy increases, more elderly people outlive their partners and continue living in the family home on their own. In addition, greater geographical mobility means that people frequently move to cities far from their relatives for work or study.

This trend has several effects on society. From an economic perspective, it has created new markets for smaller homes, single-portion meals and services aimed at individuals. However, it also puts considerable pressure on housing supply, because more homes are needed to accommodate the same number of people, which pushes up rents and property prices, particularly in large cities. A more worrying consequence is social isolation. Although many people living alone have active social lives, others, especially the elderly, can go days without meaningful contact, and loneliness can harm both physical and mental health. This may increase the demand on healthcare and social services. Finally, weaker family networks means that fewer people can rely on relatives for care and support.

In conclusion, more people live alone because of changing attitudes to marriage, increased wealth, longer lives and greater mobility. While this trend offers freedom and new business opportunities, it also contributes to housing shortages and social isolation.
samples.why: Clear position and both questions answered with extended support · logical organisation with clear topic sentences · good range of vocabulary (outlive, geographical mobility, housing supply) · mostly error-free with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
Living alone, once associated mainly with widowhood or unusual circumstances, has become a mainstream choice in many societies. This shift reflects profound changes in values, economics and demography, and while it brings certain benefits, its wider effects on society are, on balance, a cause for concern.

Changing social norms are a key driver. Marriage now tends to occur later, if at all, and living independently is widely regarded as a desirable marker of adulthood rather than a temporary stage before settling down. Greater prosperity has enabled people to act on this preference, since many can afford a home of their own. Demographic trends reinforce the pattern: as life expectancy rises, a growing number of older people outlive their partners and choose to remain in familiar surroundings rather than move in with their children. Increased mobility plays a part as well, with people relocating for work to cities where they have no family ties.

The consequences are varied. Economically, single-person households have stimulated demand for compact apartments, convenience products and services tailored to individuals, and living alone allows people to pursue careers and interests with considerable freedom. However, because more dwellings are needed to house the same population, the trend places heavy strain on housing supply and contributes to rising rents in already crowded cities. It also has environmental implications, as people living alone typically consume more energy and space per person. Most significantly, it can foster isolation. Many who live alone lead rich social lives, but for others, particularly the elderly, solitude can turn into loneliness, with damaging effects on wellbeing. As traditional family networks thin out, the responsibility for care increasingly falls on public services.

In conclusion, the rise in solo living stems from evolving attitudes, economic independence, longer lifespans and mobility. Although it offers autonomy and new economic opportunities, its impact on housing, resources and social connection means that societies need to plan for its consequences.
samples.why: Both questions fully addressed with a balanced, well-supported judgement · ideas logically sequenced across economic, environmental and social effects · wide, precise vocabulary (demography, dwellings, foster isolation) · consistently accurate complex structures.
